market_holds: Spot $7.825 (sealed baseline 2026-11-12 18:09 UTC), -31% over 20 sessions, -56.5% from the 52-week high, 5.9% above the low. Almost all of that fall is the 2026-10-26 Brazilian election gap: STNE closed $11.48 on 10-23 and $8.33 on 10-26 (Yahoo daily bars). It has been flat since, $7.39-7.85. EWZ is down 25.5%, PAGS 31%, NU 21% and INTR 45% over the same span, so the drop is Brazil beta plus a bit more, not anything specific to the company. The front-expiry straddle prices 10.9% over 8 days. That is ATM IV 84% with a 40%-of-mid spread, so it is indicative only, and the baseline's event-implied figure of 0 is an artefact of a realised vol that includes the crash day. Usual reaction: -7% (Nov 2025), about -19% (Mar 2026, on the 2026 outlook), -0.9% (May 2026), -6.65% (Aug 2026). The stock has fallen on four of the last four prints. US aggregator consensus for Q3 is $0.49-0.50 EPS and $710-715m revenue (Earnings Whispers 2026-11-04; Zacks), and FY $2.23-2.27 sits above the guide. That aggregator looks stale against the Brazilian sell-side. Itau BBA expects adjusted net income of R$571m (-11% y/y) and Safra R$553m (-13.8% y/y), per Finsiders on 2026-11-03. Itau cut its 2026 estimate by 10%. Guide: 2026 adjusted basic EPS of R$10.8-11.4, with management steering to the low end on 2026-08-13. That guide assumed a 12.5% Selic, but Copom paused at 13.75% on 2026-11-04. The 2027 guide is R$11.8-13.4. The stock trades at about 3-4x earnings (TIKR, Fool). Positioning: a BlackRock 13G/A shows 8.7% as of 09-30, and Madrone sold 750k shares at $11.90 on 10-05 (13D/A). I found no short-interest figure.
view: The quarter itself (Jul-Sep) predates the election, and the Brazilian sell-side has already marked it down to roughly R$2.35-2.40 of adjusted EPS. The thing that decides the reaction is the guide. By my arithmetic the 2026 low end of R$10.8 cannot be reached. H1 was R$4.59 (Q1 R$2.19, Q2 R$2.40), so H2 would need R$6.2, about R$3.10 a quarter, against a Q2 of R$2.40. Even a seasonally strong Q4 gets the year to about R$9.9, roughly 8% below the low end. So a 2026 cut, or an admitted miss, is close to certain. The 2027 range is also exposed to a Selic now paused at 13.75% and to the post-election macro. The question is whether that is priced. In local estimates it largely is: Itau has cut 10% and every preview names Stone as the worst-placed of the Brazilian fintechs on credit and funding. In the price it should be too: at about 3-4x earnings, 32% below its pre-election level and with no company-specific news since, the stock prices something much worse than an 8% guide trim. The upside path is capital return. The R$2bn 2026 programme is about a fifth of a roughly R$10bn market cap at today's price, and management could announce a larger repurchase into the drawdown. The downside path is the familiar one: a 2027 reset or withdrawal, rising NPLs or coverage falling again, and stale US consensus making the headline read as a miss. That pattern has hit this stock on four straight prints. These forces roughly offset, and I can find no dated datapoint released since the August call that tells me which way the release lands. I lean slightly negative on the reaction history and the 2027 exposure, but it is not a bet.

recommendation.reason: The one near-certain fact, that the 2026 EPS guide cannot be met, is already in the Brazilian sell-side's numbers (Itau -10%) and, at about 3-4x earnings after a 32% election gap, very likely in the price. I found nothing dated after the August call that shows which way tonight's release lands. Capital return could lift the stock and a 2027 reset or credit slippage could sink it, and I cannot weight one above the other on evidence.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A large new buyback (well above the R$2bn 2026 programme) with the 2027 range held would make me lean long. A withdrawal or deep cut of the 2027 range, or coverage falling below about 180%, would make me lean short.

self_critique: At 3-4x earnings, with every preview negative and the stock down on four straight prints, a 'less bad' print plus an aggressive buyback could gap the stock up 10% or more, and my slight negative lean would be wrong. Against that, the stale US consensus ($0.49 against about $0.44 implied by the Itau number at R$5.45) and a likely 2027 reset could produce another -10% open. With both tails this fat, a lean of 45 is close to a coin flip.
approach_notes: P4 (prove priced in) was the useful part: rebuilding the guide arithmetic and finding the local sell-side already below the guide stopped me from treating 'guide cut coming' as an edge. P3's fresh-data search found little because an FPI files nothing between prints.
